title: The Twelve Zodia Bound in the Sphere: how falsities-from-evil are fixed in the cosmic circuit, restrained, and traversed by Divine Truth only by economy
arc: Beginning from a disciple's question about whether the zodiacal signs are joined or separate and where the wandering stars come from, the teaching answers that all these archons are by substance mutually hostile falsities-from-evil drawn out of the Five Worlds of Darkness and bound in the sphere by the Great Artisan, made to plunder each other under stewards, and inflicting destruction on cattle, fruits, waters, and humanity according to which side of the wheel turns; the teaching closes by distinguishing the Sun and Moon, who are not of this dark dominion at all but are reckoned among them only by the necessity of the redemptive economy.
reading:
This chapter answers a single sustained question: what is the inner nature of the zodiac, the planets, and the luminaries — are they one fabric, are they each in their own place, did the Demiurge make them powers and way-leaders? The teaching's reply is severe and clarifying. The whole sphere of the natural heavens, with its twelve signs and five wanderers, is read as a fixed cosmic prison for falsities-from-evil. The signs are not "neighbors" who agree; by their very substance they are enemies and adversaries to one another, and the only thing that holds them in any order at all is the energeia of the Great Artisan — the Living Spirit in his shaping work — who has bound the whole creation and hung it within the surrounding sphere. The sphere is the wheel of natural states whose every hour casts these archons against each other so that they spend themselves in mutual plunder. Over them stand stewards, demanders, way-leaders — the divine restraining power that compels them to give back what they have seized. So the wheeling zodiac is not a sovereign machinery; it is bound captivity working under judgment.

The teaching then traces these powers to their origin. The twelve zodia were molded out of the Five Worlds of Darkness — the five modes of self-love — two signs to each world, so that the whole circle of heaven is just the proprium articulated through every quarter. Smoke, the corrupt mind, brings forth Gemini and Sagittarius; Fire, the burning of self-love, brings forth Aries and Leo; Wind, disordered perception, brings forth the airy signs; Water, the salt mingling of natural truth, brings forth Cancer and Virgo; and pure Darkness brings forth Capricorn and Scorpio. The five wandering stars are distributed in the same way: Jupiter from the Smoke (which is mind), Venus from Fire, Mars from Wind, Mercury from Water, Saturn from Darkness — each planet a particular wandering falsity rooted in one mode of the proprium. The two Anabibazons, the lunar nodes, are placed upon the mystery of Fire and Pleasure, named the Dry-One and the Moist-One, the Father and Mother of all the rest: the parental polarity of corrupt love and corrupt receptivity from which every other archon-state descends. Together the seven — five planets and the two nodes — are called outright "the makers of evil," and the teaching insists their work reaches everywhere in the All, "in the tree and in the flesh": that is, into perception (the tree as growing knowledge) and into the natural will (the flesh as proprium). Wherever a perception bears fruit or a body acts, these seven seek to corrupt the operation.

Next the teaching gives the fourfold articulation of the same twelve. They are spread out and fastened to four sides of the sphere, three to a corner — the standard elemental triplicities, but read here as the four cosmic faces of the bound darkness joined to the surrounding wheel. The teaching then shows the correspondence between each triangle's hour of plundering and its damage in the natural mind: when the fire-triangle (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) is mounted by its steward and rises to plunder, affliction strikes the cattle of the dry land — the natural affections of the will-side are scorched. When the earth-triangle (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn) plunders, it falls upon the ripenings, the figs, all the fruits of the trees — the works of life, the actualized goods of perception. When the water-triangle (Scorpio, Pisces, Cancer) plunders, the waters on the earth diminish into a year of failure — natural truth itself dries up. When the air-triangle (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius) plunders, lack and diminishing fall upon the imprint of humanity — the very seal of the human image is wasted. So the wheel is not arbitrary: each plundering touches the natural register that corresponds to its element, and the affliction of cattle, fruits, waters, and human imprint is the visible trace of one of the four faces of bound evil being permitted, in its hour, to operate upon ultimates.

The teaching closes by setting Sun and Moon utterly apart from this whole apparatus. They are "not strangers to them" — they appear in the same circuit and are reckoned along with the archons in the count — but only "on account of the necessity of the economy": because the work requires light upon it, and because they are reckoned to plunder there only as the means of liberation. They are emphatically out of this dominion, not actually of the stars and the zodia. Spiritually this is the heart of the chapter: Divine Truth in its illuminating manifestation (Sun) and in its reflective receiving (Moon) traverses the bound zodiac of dark powers as the two ships of light carrying the redemption through hostile territory, counted in among the archons only by accommodation, never belonging to them. The natural heavens are thus read as a great captivity in which the proprium has been fixed by the Great Artisan so that it can only war against itself and damage the natural register in measured ways, while the Sun and Moon, which are from the Greatness, pass through the same circuit as the very vehicles by which the captive light is gathered home. The whole sphere, in other words, is the bound state of self-love restrained for the sake of the redemption that moves through it.
